    Label clusters with representative terms

    Source: R/cluster-label.R
    sm_cluster_label.Rd

    Assigns human-readable labels to clusters by extracting representative terms. Supports TF-IDF-based extraction (default), labels from the author and indexer keywords of the corpus, YAKE keyword extraction, or labels from a chat provider via the ellmer package.

    Usage

    sm_cluster_label(
  corpus,
  method = c("tfidf", "keywords", "yake", "llm"),
  n_terms = 5L,
  llm_provider = NULL,
  min_works = NULL,
  ngram = 1:2,
  stop_terms = NULL,
  noise = 0L,
  seed = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus object with a cluster_id column in corpus$works.

    method

    Character; labelling method. One of "tfidf" (default), "keywords", "yake", or "llm".

    n_terms

    Integer; number of top terms to include in each cluster label. Defaults to 5L.

    llm_provider

    An ellmer chat provider object (e.g., ellmer::chat_openai()). Required when method = "llm", ignored otherwise. Each request uses a fresh copy; earlier turns and the object's system prompt are not used, and the object stays unchanged.

    min_works

    For "tfidf" and "keywords": the number of a cluster's works a term must occur in to enter its label. NULL (default) takes 3 or 5% of the cluster's works, whichever is more. When no term of a cluster reaches it, terms that occur in 2 of its works are used instead, as cluster_label_basis records.

    ngram

    For "tfidf": the lengths of the terms it scores, in words, as whole numbers from 1 to 3. The default 1:2 scores single words and pairs of adjacent words; 1 gives labels of single words. Two terms that overlap can be shown as the longer phrase they form (see Details). "keywords" uses it for the titles it falls back to.

    stop_terms

    Character vector of terms to leave out of the labels, such as generic words that every cluster shares; NULL (default) leaves out none. Each is compared with whole terms, ignoring case and the difference between singular and plural. Not used by "llm".

    noise

    The cluster_id that marks noise, the works no cluster claims: 0L by default, as sm_cluster_hdbscan() assigns. Noise gets no label and does not count for the labels of the other clusters. NULL labels every id as a cluster; set it for clusterings that use another noise label or a real cluster 0.

    seed

    Optional seed for sampling titles with a chat provider. The session random state is restored afterwards. NULL uses the session random stream as before. Used only by method = "llm".

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    The input corpus with two columns added to corpus$works, in place of earlier ones:

    cluster_label

    The terms of the work's cluster joined with "; ", the best first; NA for noise, for works without a cluster and for clusters that got no label.

    cluster_label_basis

    How the label was made: "tfidf" or "keywords" when every term occurs in at least min_works of the cluster's works; "tfidf (relaxed)" or "keywords (relaxed)" when no term reached min_works, so that the terms occur in at least 2 works; "tfidf (fallback)" or "tfidf (fallback, relaxed)" when method = "keywords" found no keyword in 2 or more of the cluster's works and took the terms of its titles; "yake" or "llm" for these methods; NA where cluster_label is NA.

    Details

    Noise and clusters without a label: works whose cluster_id is NA or noise get no label from any method, and the "tfidf" and "keywords" methods leave them out of the works that make a term common or rare in the corpus. A cluster whose works share no term, such as a cluster of a single work, gets no label either, with a message.

    TF-IDF method: Splits the titles and abstracts of the works into terms of ngram words. A term's score in a cluster is the share of the cluster's works that contain it times log(N / n), where N is the number of clustered works and n the number of them that contain the term. As the score counts works, not occurrences, and a term must occur in at least min_works works of the cluster, a term that one paper repeats cannot name a cluster. The n_terms terms with the highest scores form the label; ties go to the term that occurs more often in the cluster, then to the first in alphabetical order. A longer term takes the place of a shorter one it contains when it occurs in at least 40% of the shorter term's works ("cancer" gives way to "testicular cancer", and to "metastatic testicular cancer" only if that also occurs in 40% of the works with "cancer"), and a term contained in one already chosen is skipped. When a term overlaps one already chosen, as "heat illness" overlaps "exertional heat", the phrase they form ("exertional heat illness") counts as a longer term that contains both, also beyond the lengths in ngram, if it occurs in enough of the cluster's works to be a term of the label; so one phrase does not fill two places of a label.

    Words of fewer than 3 characters, numbers and stop words are left out, and no term spans one of them, the end of a sentence or clause, or the border between title and abstract. The stop words of every work are the English ones of tidytext::stop_words, plus the Snowball list of the stopwords package for the work's own language in works$language, given as a name such as "German", an ISO 639-1 code such as "de" or an ISO 639-2 code such as "ger". Works without a language get the English list only, and the lists of other languages are never pooled, so German stop words such as "war" or "die" stay in English text. Without the stopwords package, or for a language it has no list for, only the English list is used, with a message.

    Singular and plural count as one term: a final "ies" becomes "y", and a final "s" is dropped after a letter other than s, i, u, o, a and y, so "fractures" counts with "fracture" and "ticks" with "tick", while "diagnosis", "virus", "class" and "days" stay as they are. A possessive "'s" is dropped as well, and words such as "species", "series", "diabetes", "measles" or "aids" are kept as written, as are names of fields such as "logistics", "genetics", "genomics" or "pediatrics", which would otherwise count with the adjectives "logistic", "genetic", "genomic" or "pediatric". A label shows each term in the spelling the cluster's works use most often.

    Keyword method: The same scoring on the author keywords and the indexer keywords (such as Keywords Plus or MeSH) in corpus$concepts, the families "author_keyword" and "indexer_keyword" of sm_concept_vocabularies(). Keywords are compared ignoring case, with hyphens read as spaces and plurals folded as above, and containment is checked on whole words; keywords that overlap form no phrase. A work counts once for each keyword, however many of its vocabularies give it. A keyword is shown as an author keyword spells it, or else in lower case. A cluster without a keyword in at least 2 of its works gets the TF-IDF terms of its titles instead; when the clustered works have no such keywords at all, every cluster does, with a message.

    YAKE method: Uses a simplified YAKE-like scoring based on term frequency, position, and spread across works within each cluster, with the stop words of the TF-IDF method.

    LLM method: Sends titles and abstracts of each cluster to an LLM with a prompt asking for a concise topical label. Requires the ellmer package and a configured provider.

    See also

    Other clustering: sm_cluster_evolution(), sm_cluster_hdbscan(), sm_cluster_kmeans(), sm_cluster_leiden()

    Examples

    # \donttest{
corpus <- sm_example_corpus(with_embeddings = TRUE)
corpus <- sm_cluster_kmeans(corpus, k = 5)
#> ✔ K-means clustering complete.
#> ℹ 5 clusters, sizes range from 27 to 49.
corpus <- sm_cluster_label(corpus, method = "tfidf", n_terms = 3L)
#> ✔ 5 clusters labelled using "tfidf" method.
unique(corpus$works[, c("cluster_id", "cluster_label",
                        "cluster_label_basis")])
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   cluster_id cluster_label                                   cluster_label_basis
#>        <int> <chr>                                           <chr>              
#> 1          5 drug resistance; clinical outcomes; cross sect… tfidf              
#> 2          1 cohort study; investigates drug; machine learn… tfidf              
#> 3          3 meta analysis; spatial transcriptomics; prospe… tfidf              
#> 4          4 meta analysis; investigates spatial transcript… tfidf              
#> 5          2 trial approaches; cross sectional study; immun… tfidf              

# keyword labels: the real-use example corpus grouped by journal category
fix <- readRDS(sm_example_files("example_realuse_corpus.rds"))
fix$works$cluster_id <- match(fix$works$field, unique(fix$works$field))
fix <- sm_cluster_label(fix, method = "keywords", n_terms = 3L)
#> ✔ 8 clusters labelled using "keywords" method.
unique(fix$works[, c("field", "cluster_label", "cluster_label_basis")])
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   field                                       cluster_label  cluster_label_basis
#>   <chr>                                       <chr>          <chr>              
#> 1 Microbiology                                transmission;… keywords           
#> 2 Medicine, General & Internal                injury; hemor… keywords           
#> 3 Public, Environmental & Occupational Health zoonotic surv… keywords           
#> 4 Infectious Diseases                         antibodies; o… keywords           
#> 5 Toxicology                                  workforce; ed… keywords           
#> 6 Physiology                                  recruits; exe… keywords           
#> 7 Surgery                                     hemorrhage co… keywords           
#> 8 Emergency Medicine                          damage contro… keywords           
# }
